items.title: Samsung confirms the best new thing about its SmartTag 3 trackers
items.summary: Broad Android support is official for the SmartTag 3.
items.body: TL;DR Past Samsung SmartTag trackers have only supported monitoring through Samsung Galaxy phones. The just-announced SmartTag 3 formally extended that support to iOS devices. Samsung now clarifies that other Android models are getting access, as well. Samsung just got finished introducing its new tablets last week, announcing the Galaxy Tab S12 Plus and Ultra . And while these were assuredly the stars of the company’s launch event, we also got to meet them alongside the latest generation of a familiar Samsung accessory — its SmartTag 3 . We were already excited about the much broader device support we’re getting this time around, and now Samsung is clarifying exactly how expansive that really is. Historically, Samsung’s trackers have been a bit limited in terms of their device support. While you could slap a SmartTag on anything you wanted to track, the SmartTag2, for example, worked with “Galaxy S24, Galaxy S25, Galaxy S26, Galaxy Z Fold, Galaxy Z Flip, and Galaxy A series smartphones running the latest version of the SmartThings app.” If you had a different phone, you were officially out of luck.

items.title: Smartwatches are struggling to connect with Strava
items.summary: A smartwatch-to-Strava glitch is frustrating the fitness community.
items.body: Credit: Kaitlyn Cimino / Android Authority TL;DR Strava is reportedly having trouble syncing with smartwatches. Users are experiencing the issue on Galaxy, Garmin, and Apple devices. It’s unclear what the cause of the issue is. After a run, swim, ride, and so on, you shouldn’t have to even think about sending over your workout data from your smartwatch to Strava . Syncing your device with the app automatically uploads this recorded information to your profile. However, a new pesky bug appears to be getting in the way. We’re seeing multiple reports on Reddit about an issue with Strava. According to the affected users, they are being greeted by an error message when attempting to connect their smartwatch to the app. The syncing issue reportedly persists whether you’re using the Samsung Health app or Health Connect.

items.title: Samsung may have found a smart way to speed up Galaxy S27 Ultra charging
items.summary: The trick could be sustaining higher charging speeds for longer.
items.body: TL;DR The Galaxy S27 Ultra is rumored to keep the same 60W charging rating as the S26 Ultra. But Samsung may make that 60W work harder, potentially cutting charging times despite a larger battery. It’s still unclear whether the improvements will remain exclusive to the S27 Ultra. Apple gave Samsung an unusual taste of its own numbers game this year. The iPhone 18 Pro Max arrived with a 5,391mAh rated battery, edging past the Galaxy S26 Ultra’s 5,000mAh cell, while Apple also substantially improved wired charging to match Samsung. While the next Galaxy Ultra is already rumored to respond with a 5,700mAh battery , Samsung may have another trick planned for getting that larger cell topped up faster. According to leaker WalleGalaxy , the Galaxy S27 Ultra will retain the S26 Ultra’s 60W charging rating. However, Samsung is reportedly working on charging optimizations that would let the phone hold higher power levels longer during the early stages of a charge.

items.title: The first national ban on smart glasses could happen soon
items.summary: This country is considering a ban on smart glasses in some areas.
items.body: Credit: Meta TL;DR Norway’s government is proposing a temporary ban on smart glasses in some locations. The ban would apply to areas where “privacy is particularly important,” like schools, healthcare facilities, and fitness centers. The temporary ban would give the government time to decide which type of devices would be affected and whether permanent regulation is needed. Smart glasses are the hot new category that every major tech company is trying to jump on. Just last week, Samsung took one step closer to launching its first effort into the segment. However, as smart glasses continue to inch toward going mainstream, it’s becoming increasingly difficult to look past the growing concerns surrounding the technology, namely privacy. Now, one country is confronting those concerns by taking matters into its hands. According to The Associated Press , Norway is proposing a temporary ban on smart glasses. This would not be a blanket ban, but rather a ban in certain locations. It’s reported that the country wants the proposal sent to parliament “as soon as possible.”

items.title: Samsung’s Android 17 rollout is picking up the pace in the US
items.summary: The wait for One UI 9 is ending for more Galaxy owners in the US.
items.body: TL;DR Samsung is expanding the stable One UI 9 update to the Galaxy S25 series, Galaxy Z Fold 7, and Galaxy Z Flip 7 in the US. The Android 17 update is reaching both carrier-locked and unlocked models, though availability still varies by carrier and device. One UI 9 adds new Galaxy AI features, more Quick Panel customization, privacy upgrades, Samsung Health improvements, and device-specific changes for the foldables. Samsung’s stable One UI 9 rollout has been gathering pace over the past few weeks, but owners of some of the company’s biggest 2025 flagships outside South Korea have mostly been watching from the sidelines. That is finally changing, with the Android 17 update now reaching more Galaxy S25 series, Galaxy Z Fold 7, and Galaxy Z Flip 7 models in the US. This comes about a week after Samsung started updating these devices in South Korea. The US rollout initially appeared on a handful of carrier variants, but it is now expanding to both carrier-locked and unlocked models.

items.title: The Googlebooks include a file transfer trick you probably didn’t know about
items.summary: Quick Access lets you seamlessly transfer files to and from a Googlebook and Android phone.
items.body: TL;DR The recently launched range of Googlebooks includes a new Quick Access feature for instant browsing or copying files between your phone and laptop. However, Quick Access works only for files under 200MB, with Google recommending Quick Share for larger items. Googlebooks will also include Files AI, which gives you instant descriptions of files without opening them. The recently announced lineup of Googlebooks is here, with pre-order shipments beginning yesterday. Like most new releases, the software still has aspects that are new to us. We learned about some of the Googlebook’s limitations earlier today, and now we’re getting new info on some software features that may have flown under the radar. After poring over a reviewer’s guide Google prepared for the launch of the new laptop line, we’re learning about Quick Access. This feature lets you seamlessly control files between your paired Android phone and the Googlebook. “Browse, open, and transfer files between your phone and your Googlebook as easily as a local drive,” the document says.

items.title: Forget booking restaurant reservations — Gemini could soon call your mom for you
items.summary: Gemini could expand from annoying businesses on the phone to annoying your friends.
items.body: TL;DR Call for Me on Pixel 11 phones makes it easy to have Gemini call businesses on your behalf. Google could be planning to expand that functionality to also support interactions with friends and family Users could have Gemini call your contacts to share information with them, or ask questions and report the answers back to you. How many phone calls have you put off just because dealing with another person can feel so tedious? AI has already promised to automate plenty of thankless tasks in our lives, and for a certain kind of person, maybe one of the most appealing possibilities there is making phone calls on our behalf. We just saw Google introduce Call for Me on the Pixel 11 series, and now we’re already getting an early look at what could be a big new expansion for what it’s capable of doing. items.title: This app gives Wear OS the Pixel music feature Apple already copied
items.summary: A new Wear OS app puts Pixel’s Now Playing where it always belonged.
items.body: TL;DR Now On Wrist brings your Pixel’s Now Playing results directly to a Wear OS smartwatch. It can show detected songs through notifications, a watch face complication, and a dedicated Wear OS tile. The app is available now on Google Play and works with Wear OS 3.0 or newer. Hearing a great song and having your Pixel identify it automatically is handy, but checking the result still usually means reaching for your phone. That feels a little clunky when you’re already wearing a smartwatch, which is where a new app called Now On Wrist comes in. It fixes that disconnect by bringing your Pixel’s Now Playing results directly to Wear OS. Now On Wrist doesn’t actually turn your smartwatch into a music-recognition device. Instead, it relies on the ambient music recognition happening on your phone, including Google’s Now Playing feature, and sends the identified song and artist to your wrist.

items.title: This iOS calendar app is side-stepping Android to embrace Googlebooks
items.summary: Will we be seeing more Googlebook exclusives further down the road?
items.body: TL;DR Fantastical launched as an iOS calendar app 15 years ago. It’s now finally coming to Google’s mobile devices with a Googlebook port. There’s a free version available, as well as several premium paid tiers. In a perfect world, the software we want to use would be available across all major platforms — but that’s just not the reality we live in. For multiple reasons, access is still a problem, and we’re always happy to see when a developer opens its doors to a new platform. Most of the time, that’s an iOS-only app finally becoming available for Android phones . Today, however, we might be looking at the first time ever an app skipped Android proper in order to launch a Googlebook edition. Fantastical is a powerful scheduling solution that got its start on Apple’s platforms, before eventually expanding to Windows. But in the 15 years it’s been around, the calendar app hasn’t been available for Google’s ecosystem. While it’s still not making the leap to Android phones and tablets — at least not yet — Fantastical is finally dipping a toe in the Google pool as developer Flexibits announces plans for a native Googlebook release.

items.title: Want cheaper flights? Google says this is the best time to book one
items.summary: Cheap flights care more about timing than Tuesdays.
items.body: TL;DR Google says domestic flights have historically been cheapest around 39 days before departure, while international fares hit their lowest around 89 days out. The idea that Tuesday is the best day to book is largely a myth, with the cheapest booking day saving only about 1.4% versus the most expensive. Changing when and how you fly matters more: weekday travel can save up to 20% domestically, while nonstop flights cost around 20% more than connecting options. Booking a flight can sometimes feel like a gamble. You find a fare that looks reasonable, but instead of booking it, you start wondering whether it’ll be cheaper tomorrow. But wait too long, and you could end up paying even more. Google already tries to make that decision easier with its travel tools, and now it’s sharing more data on when to book. If you already know your destination and travel dates, Google Flights and AI Mode in Search can show you the “cheapest time to book,” helping you understand whether current fares are on the lower side or if prices could change in the coming days.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Selfie at Vera Rubin Ridge Explanation: On sol 1943 of its journey of exploration across the surface of Mars, the Curiosity Rover recorded this selfie at the south rim of Vera Rubin Ridge. Of course a sol is a Martian solar day , about 40 minutes longer than an Earth day. Curiosity’s sol 1943 corresponds to Earth date January 23, 2018. Also composed as an interactive 360 degree VR , the mosaicked panorama combines 61 exposures taken by the small car-sized rover’s Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI). YouTube Shorts have never exactly been a fan-favorite feature. From users wanting Shorts to be a standalone app, to YouTube itself letting users set their daily Shorts feed limit to zer o, there’s no shortage of signs pointing to how unhappy many users are with how aggressively short-form video has been pushed across the platform. PlayStation 3 emulation on Android made major strides in recent months thanks to the ARMSX3 app. However, one potential issue is that PS3 games can hog a ton of space on your Android device. Fortunately, a recent ARMSX3 update helps address this issue. The team behind ARMSX3 recently released v1.0.6 of the emulator on GitHub , and it now supports CHD disc images. CHD (Compressed Hunks of Data) is a compression format that delivers smaller file sizes than conventional ISOs.
